activities.anchor: The shared factors act as controls by construction
activities.caption: file each design claim under the right Mill descendant
activities.name: cpMssdSort

config.prompt: Two designs, two causal questions — file each claim under the design it describes:

items.label: countries alike on colonial history, resources, religion and income — differing on the suspected cause
hunts factors sufficient to produce the outcome in a given context
UK first-past-the-post vs Netherlands proportional representation — the electoral formula is the standing suspect
countries unalike in almost everything that share the same outcome
durable democracy in Costa Rica, Mauritius and Uruguay — no shared region, religion, or colonial ruler

config.why: Method of difference versus method of agreement at country scale — and real research typically runs both directions.

activities.caption: one line of this case-selection briefing is wrong
activities.name: cpSelectSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's case-selection briefing is wrong — click it:
lines: Select cases to vary the outcome — a comparison set with no variation cannot separate cause from ubiquity.
Select on the regression line for quantitative pairing — cases typical of the relationship you mean to explain.
Deviant cases — outliers — are the first to discard, since the model should already explain them.
A well-chosen pair of countries can be decisive where randomisation is impossible.
Comparisons are only as good as the choice of cases — selection, not statistics, carries the inference.
config.correction: Outliers are reserved for mechanism-hunting: what the model cannot explain is where its story lives or dies.
config.why: Typical cases establish the relationship; the deviant case is where the mechanism gets tested — discarding it throws away the model's sharpest test.

activities.anchor: The case study earns its place three ways
activities.caption: rebuild the case-study defence, step by step
activities.name: cpCaseOrder

config.prompt: How one case becomes an inference engine — assemble the sequence:
items: Hypothesis generation: deep knowledge of one case surfaces variables no dataset codes
Mechanism testing: regression says X predicts Y — only inside a case can you watch X produce Y
Process tracing formalises the watching: each piece of evidence is a Bayesian update — likely if the hypothesis is true versus if it is false
Hoop and smoking-gun tests specified in advance: evidence the theory says must exist, evidence only that theory predicts
Crucial-case logic: an easy case failed, or a least-likely case passed, carries unusual weight
config.why: The sequence is cumulative — each step is what makes the next legitimate, ending with a single case able to overturn a generalisation.

activities.caption: pair each classic with its comparative design
activities.name: cpClassicsMatch

config.prompt: The classics as design exemplars — pair each work with what it did:

pairs.right: most-similar analysis across France 1789, Russia 1917, China 1949 — state crises, not misery, cause revolution
typological comparison over eight countries — 'no bourgeoisie, no democracy', routes rather than a single cause
every regime since 1950: above an income threshold, no democracy has fallen — preservation, not creation
UK versus Netherlands: the electoral formula is the standing suspect for party-system shape
dismantled a generation of revolution literature that never looked at the non-revolutions

config.why: Each durable theory was built by a recognisable design — which is why the canonical works double as methods manuals.

activities.caption: bet on which way the development–democracy arrow points
activities.name: cpDevPredict

config.q: Rich countries are democracies — Przeworski and Limongi's large-N analysis of every regime since 1950 found the arrow mostly runs how?
choices: preservation — development keeps existing democracies alive
irrelevance — the correlation is a data artefact
config.why: Above roughly a per-capita income threshold, no democracy has fallen: democracies are made by contingency and preserved by development.

activities.caption: drag the divider — the mixed-methods division of labour
activities.name: cpMixedCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — what each half of the mixed-methods answer does:

before.label: large-N side
before.text: Screen variables, establish scope, find the puzzles — regression across roughly 200 countries, where every added control eats a case.

after.label: small-N side
after.text: Establish mechanisms and adjudicate among competing stories — paired comparison and process tracing, with QCA as the bridge: set-theoretic logic over a dozen cases.

config.why: Most political causation is 'X matters only with Y' — conjunctural — which neither regression's average effects nor Mill's single factor captures cleanly.

activities.caption: file each point under QCA's virtues or its costs
activities.name: cpQcaSort

config.prompt: The QCA balance sheet — file each point on the right side:

items.label: explicit sufficiency-and-necessity logic suited to policy configurations
transparency — every case-to-row calibration is auditable
finds equifinality: multiple different routes to the same outcome
limited cases force limited conditions — rows outrun cases fast
calibration is judgement-laden: the fuzzy memberships are the researcher's claims
conclusions are set-relations, not effect sizes — which recipe, not how much each ingredient adds

config.why: The mature practice pairs it with its rivals: QCA for configurations, regression for magnitudes, process tracing for mechanisms.

activities.anchor: wars, depressions and crises open windows
activities.caption: walk a critical juncture and the path it locks in
activities.name: cpJunctureBranch

config.root: 1945: a war has just ended. Structure is relaxed and agency weighs most. Walk the settlement and what it does for decades.

start.text: The formative moment is now. What gets decided while the juncture lasts?

choices.label: Build a comprehensive welfare architecture now
Wait — decide when the fiscal picture is clearer

locked.text: The choice creates increasing returns: complementarities, sunk investments, constituencies built on the institution — switching costs rise with every year, the QWERTY logic applied to polities.

choices.label: How does change still happen afterwards?

spent.text: Junctures close fast. Without a decision the crisis passes and the old structure reasserts itself — a formative moment spent unspent.

choices.label: Watch what a taken juncture produces instead

gradual.text: Later change is gradual, by Streeck and Thelen's taxonomy: layering (accretion on the institution), drift (erosion of its environment), conversion (repurposing to new ends) — formal continuity coexisting with substantive change.

config.why: Critical junctures explain decades of divergence from single formative moments — and path dependence specifies when comparison is meaningful: within a path versus across paths.
